blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) is monitoring a low pressure area (LPA) inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), while a storm outside the monitoring region has intensified into a super typhoon. In its weather update as of 8 p.m. on Thursday, October 29, 2026, PAGASA said the weather disturbance, identified as LPA 10c, is unlikely to develop into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.
